MOD = 998244353

def count_chaotic_merges(x, y):
    n, m = len(x), len(y)
    
    # dp[i][j] will store the number of ways to merge x[:i] and y[:j] into a chaotic string
    dp = [[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    
    # Base case: empty strings can be merged into an empty chaotic string in one way
    dp[0][0] = 1
    
    # Fill the dp table
    for i in range(n + 1):
        for j in range(m + 1):
            if i > 0:
                dp[i][j] += dp[i - 1][j]
                if j > 0 and x[i - 1] != y[j - 1]:
                    dp[i][j] += dp[i - 1][j - 1]
            if j > 0:
                dp[i][j] += dp[i][j - 1]
                if i > 0 and x[i - 1] != y[j - 1]:
                    dp[i][j] += dp[i - 1][j]
            
            dp[i][j] %= MOD
    
    # Sum up all the ways to merge all possible substrings of x and y
    total = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            total += dp[i][j]
            total %= MOD
    
    return total
